items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend part B of chapter 173 of the laws of 2013 relating to the
issuance of securitized restructuring bonds to refinance the outstanding debt
of the Long Island power authority, in relation to the utility debt
securitization authority; and in relation to permitting the issuance of
securitized restructuring bonds to finance system resiliency costs; and to
amend the public authorities law, in relation to certain contracts by the Long
Island power authority
items.lawCode: Amd Part B §§2, 3 & 4, Chap 173 of 2013; amd §1020-cc, Pub Auth L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6455

SPONSOR: KAMINSKY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend part B of chapter 173 of the laws of 2013 relating to
the issuance of  securitized  restructuring  bonds  to  refinance  the
outstanding debt of the Long Island power authority,  in  relation  to
the  utility  debt  securitization authority;  and  in relation to
permitting the issuance of securitized restructuring bonds to finance
system resiliency costs; and to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to certain contracts by the Long Island power authority

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would permit the issuance by the Utility Debt Securitization
Authority (UDSA) of additional securitized restructuring to fund costs
of improvements to the Long Island Power Authority's (LIPA) transmission
and distribution system.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 establishes the legislative findings.

Section 2 amends chapter 173 of the laws of 2013, to allow bonds to fund
system resiliency costs.

Section 3 amends the definition of "restructuring bonds" so that bonds
issued by UDSA shall have a final maturity of no later than thirty years
from their date of issue.

Section 4 adds a new definition of "system resiliency costs," which
includes rebuilding and improving the transmission and distribution
systems to increase resiliency.

Section 5 grants comptroller oversight on bond issuances for LIPA.

Section 6 amends the $4.5 billion cap on UDSA bonds so that the cap
applies to the aggregate principal amount outstanding, rather than the
total amount issued.

Section 7 makes conforming amendments.

Section 8 gives the comptroller oversight of contracts over $500,000,
except in emergency instances.  Action 9. Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Due to an increase in extreme weather events caused by climate change,
energy providers need to take proactive steps to reduce vulnerabilities
in our energy system's infrastructure. Such actions are crucial to
ensure people have reliable access to electricity, even during storms,
which has not been this case recently as seen by problems occurring
during Tropical Storm Isaias. Upgrades must be made to harden and
protect this essential infrastructure from rising flood levels,
increased wind speeds, and unpredictable storms.  This bill will allow
the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) to take advantage of the current
low cost of borrowing, in order to finance system resilience upgrades
and improvements. With interest rates low, LIPA will be able to save
ratepayers over six hundred million dollars over a twenty-year period by
making these investments now and in a fiscally responsible manner.
However, it is also important there is proper oversight of this expanded
borrowing authority so that the state can protect ratepayers by ensuring
LIPA makes investments equitably and transparently. This bill achieves
that by granting the Comptroller oversight of certain bonding activ-
ities, as well as contracts made between LIPA and PSEG-LI. The increased
oversight will help guarantee investments are done in a prudent and
efficient manner, while also holding LIPA to a similar standard as other
public authorities, like the New York Power Authority.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Savings to ratepayers for refinancing bonds.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill would take effect immediately.
